newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mayors oppose new air rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mayors oppose new air rules.

text.p: U.S. mayors voted on Tuesday to oppose a plan by the Environmental Protection Agency to set strict new limits on smog and soot, saying the proposed standards could jeopardise other government programmes.
The U.S. Conference of Mayors, meeting in San Francisco, approved the controversial resolution after a brief debate. The resolution faced little opposition.
"I don't think there's a mayor anywhere that doesn't want clean air," said Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer, who introduced the resolution. "In this instance, I think we've gone too far too fast."
The resolution calls for the EPA to stick with current standards for smog-forming ozone and fine particles rather than tightening them as it proposed last November.

"The proposed standards have the potential to jeopardise progress toward other federal priorities that are equally important to achieving sustainable communities, such as the revitalisation of our cities, empowerment zone initiatives, job creation and improved technologies," the resolution said.

Republicans have urged the Clinton administration not to go ahead with the proposed rules until more research is done on the health impact of fine particles. Democrats are divided over whether to support stricter clean air standards.
